title: Layer-selective chirality switch in bilayer graphene intercalated by Janus monolayers
abstract: We predict that intercalating bilayer graphene with nonmagnetic WSSe or magnetic MnSSe Janus monolayers induces a layer-selective switch of the in-plane Rashba spin texture, resulting in opposite spin current directions in the top and bottom graphene layers. First-principles calculations reveal that both Janus monolayers decouple the two graphene layers while simultaneously inducing opposite signs of the proximity-induced Rashba spin-orbit coupling in each. Tight-binding modeling of the proximitized layers, combined with Rashba-Edelstein charge-to-spin conversion calculations, confirms that the spin current direction can be independently controlled by gating the top or bottom graphene layer. Bilayer graphene intercalated by Janus monolayers thus represents a promising platform for gate-tunable, layer-selective spintronic devices.
summary: This theoretical study predicts that sandwiching bilayer graphene between Janus monolayers like WSSe or MnSSe creates a platform for advanced spintronics. The key mechanism involves the monolayer inducing opposite signs of Rashba SOC in the top and bottom layers, allowing researchers to independently switch spin current directions by applying gate voltages.
main_problem: The goal is to design gate-tunable, layer-selective spintronic devices by independently controlling the spin current direction in the top and bottom layers of bilayer graphene.
main_result: Intercalating bilayer graphene with Janus monolayers (WSSe or MnSSe) induces opposite signs of proximity-induced Rashba SOC in each layer, enabling independent control over spin currents via electrostatic gating.
method: The study uses first-principles DFT calculations to derive parameters for an effective tight-binding model, followed by linear response theory and Rashba-Edelstein conversion calculations.
model_or_system: The system is bilayer graphene ($	ext{Gr}$) sandwiched between a Janus monolayer ($	ext{WSSe}$ or $	ext{MnSSe}$). The low-energy physics is modeled using two independent, proximitized graphene layers described by effective Hamiltonians incorporating orbital, intrinsic SOC, and Rashba SOC terms.
key_observables: Rashba-Edelstein coefficient ($\alpha_{	ext{REE}}$), spin current direction, layer-resolved band structure, and chemical potential shifts.
important_parameters: The proximity-induced Rashba SOC signs, the exchange coupling parameters ($\Delta_A, \Delta_B$) for magnetic cases, and gate voltages applied to individual layers.
main_assumptions: The low-energy physics is assumed to be described by two independent graphene layers due to the decoupling effect; the $	ext{MnSSe}$ magnetic configuration uses an out-of-plane antiferromagnetic model case.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows how a charge current generates spin accumulations in opposite directions. Figure 2 confirms decoupled Dirac cones and layer-resolved band structures for both heterostructures.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by establishing the physical system (Janus intercalation), deriving effective Hamiltonians incorporating proximity effects, calculating key transport coefficients like $\alpha_{	ext{REE}}$, and demonstrating that opposite SOC signs lead to independent spin current control via gating.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter spintronics, the concept of using engineered interfaces (Janus materials) to induce controllable, layer-specific spin-orbit coupling is relevant to understanding topological phenomena in low-dimensional quantum systems.
